issues.title: [US-05] Complete first-login counsellor onboarding
issues.body:
**Requirement ID:** `US-05`
**Priority:** Must-have · **Estimate:** 4 SP · **Status:** Baseline
**Epic:** A – Authentication and Accounts · **Role:** Career Counsellor

## User outcome
Complete first-login counsellor onboarding

## Acceptance summary
A new counsellor is directed to professional-profile and verification setup before publishing services.

## Purpose
Support US-05 by routing a Career Counsellor's first login into professional-profile and verification setup before services can be published, so that Erika and David are guided through the required setup steps instead of having to find them themselves.

## Scope
- Backend exposes the counsellor's onboarding state (profile saved, verification submitted) so the app can route after login.
- On first successful login, the app routes a Career Counsellor to an onboarding flow presenting professional-profile setup (US-30) and LinkedIn verification submission (US-31) as required steps (Requirements.md US-05).
- Service publishing is not offered until both steps are complete; the app shows an English explanation of what remains.
- Once onboarding is complete, subsequent logins route to the regular counsellor area (US-06).

**Out of scope**
- The profile form itself (US-30), LinkedIn URL submission and validation (US-31), and verification status display (US-32).
- Service creation and My Services, and backend rejection of service creation by a counsellor who has not completed onboarding — enforced in US-34 (eligibility), which depends on this story.
- First-login diagnose triage for Job Seekers — US-09 to US-13, outside the active backlog.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given Erika has registered as a Career Counsellor and has never logged in, when she logs in successfully for the first time, then the app navigates to the counsellor onboarding flow showing professional-profile setup and verification submission as required steps, not to the regular counsellor area.
- [ ] Given Erika has not completed both onboarding steps, when she views the onboarding flow after login, then it lists which of profile setup and verification submission remain, shows an English message that both must be completed before services can be published, and offers no route to service creation.
- [ ] Given a counsellor account that has not completed onboarding, when the app requests that account's onboarding state from the backend, then the response reports profile setup and verification submission as incomplete.
- [ ] Given David has saved his professional profile and submitted his LinkedIn URL, when he logs in again, then the app routes him to the regular counsellor area and no longer shows the onboarding gate.
- [ ] Given the backend has not yet returned Erika's onboarding state, when the app is deciding where to route her after login, then it shows a loading state and displays neither the onboarding flow nor the counsellor area until the state is received.

## Evidence
_Fill in when the story closes: link the PR, the tests and the device recordings that prove the acceptance criteria._
- [ ] PR: onboarding state, first-login routing, and publish gate merged into `dev`
- [ ] Test: AT-US-05-1 (first login routes to onboarding), AT-US-05-2 (publish gated until profile saved and verification submitted), AT-US-05-3 (completed onboarding routes to counsellor area) passing
- [ ] Integration test: onboarding-state endpoint reflects profile saved and URL submitted (BE)
- [ ] Screen recording: first-login onboarding on iOS and Android
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on this issue

## Dependencies
Blocked by: US-04 (#7), US-06 (#9), US-30 (#24), US-31 (#25)

## Sub-tasks
_Suggested split for the sub-team; convert to sub-issues at sprint planning._
- [ ] BE: Expose onboarding-state endpoint for counsellor accounts
- [ ] FE: Route first login to onboarding; show remaining steps
- [ ] QA: First-login, gate, and completed-onboarding tests both platforms

## Assumptions and open decisions
- Onboarding is complete when the profile is saved and a LinkedIn URL is submitted; whether service creation also requires verified (not pending) status is undecided (CLIENT-01; R-02 suggests allowing drafts while pending) and must be agreed with US-34's eligibility rule.
- The LinkedIn approach is still open (25 Aug 2026 minutes); if account linking is chosen, the verification step in onboarding changes.

## Definition of Ready / Done
See `backlog.md` §6 and §7.

## Traceability

issues.title: [US-70] Reset a forgotten password securely
issues.body:
**Requirement ID:** `US-70`
**Priority:** Must-have · **Estimate:** 5 SP · **Status:** Baseline
**Epic:** A – Authentication and Accounts · **Role:** Any user

## User outcome
Reset a forgotten password securely

## Acceptance summary
A registered user can request a secure reset link and set a new valid password without exposing account existence.

## Purpose
Support US-70 by letting a registered user request a reset link and set a new valid password without the app or API revealing whether an email is registered, so that Sam and Erika can regain access to their accounts securely.

## Scope
- Forgot-password entry from the login screen with an email field and submit; always shows the same generic English confirmation.
- Backend reset-request endpoint generates a reset token for a registered email and sends a reset link by email; the response is identical for unregistered emails (backlog US-70).
- Set-new-password screen opened from the reset link: new password and confirmation, submitted with the token to the backend.
- Backend validates the token, replaces the stored password hash, and rejects invalid or expired tokens (NFR-04).
- App shows success and navigates to login only after backend confirmation (Requirements.md §4 NFR).

**Out of scope**
- Changing the password while logged in — not in the baseline.
- Recovery by other channels (SMS, security questions) or changing the account email — not in the baseline.
- In-app notification centre — US-60 and US-61, outside the active backlog.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given Sam is on the login screen, when he taps Forgot password and submits his registered email, then the backend creates a reset token and sends a reset link to that email, and the app shows a generic English confirmation that instructions were sent if an account exists.
- [ ] Given an email that is not registered, when Sam submits it on the forgot-password screen, then the app shows the identical confirmation message and the backend response is indistinguishable from the registered case.
- [ ] Given Sam opens a valid reset link, when he enters a new valid password with a matching confirmation and the backend confirms, then the stored password hash is replaced, the app shows success and navigates to login, and the old password no longer authenticates.
- [ ] Given a reset token that is expired, already used, or altered, when Sam submits a new password with it, then the backend rejects the request, the password is unchanged, and the app shows an error rather than success.
- [ ] Given the reset submission is in flight or fails with a network or server error, when Sam waits on the set-new-password screen, then the app shows a processing or error state and does not show success or navigate to login.

## Evidence
_Fill in when the story closes: link the PR, the tests and the device recordings that prove the acceptance criteria._
- [ ] PR: reset request, token handling, and set-new-password screen merged into `dev`
- [ ] Test: AT-US-70-1 (registered email: link sent, generic confirmation), AT-US-70-2 (unregistered email: identical response), AT-US-70-3 (valid token sets new password; old password fails), AT-US-70-4 (expired, used, or altered token rejected) passing
- [ ] Integration test: token lifecycle and hash replacement (BE)
- [ ] Screen recording: forgot-password through to successful login on iOS and Android
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded on this issue

## Dependencies
Blocked by: US-02 (#5), US-06 (#9)

## Sub-tasks
_Suggested split for the sub-team; convert to sub-issues at sprint planning._
- [ ] BE: Reset-request and reset-confirm endpoints with token lifecycle
- [ ] BE: Outbound email delivery for the reset link
- [ ] FE: Forgot-password and set-new-password screens with generic confirmation
- [ ] QA: Token validity, expiry, and enumeration tests on both platforms

## Assumptions and open decisions
- A token lifetime and single-use handling are implied by 'secure reset link' and NFR-04, but no duration is specified; the team must agree it before the story is Ready.
- The email delivery provider and how the emailed link opens the app's set-new-password screen (deep link versus a code entered in the app) are implementation decisions to record in the design notebook.
- The password validity rule is the same undecided rule as US-01/US-02; whether other active sessions are invalidated after a reset is not stated in any source.

## Definition of Ready / Done
See `backlog.md` §6 and §7.

## Traceability
Baseline: `backlog.md` · Wiki: https://github.com/swen90014-2026-sm2/SWEN90014-2026-CSD-Koala/wiki/Requirements

issues.title: [US-27] Control profile visibility
issues.body:
**Requirement ID:** `US-27`
**Priority:** Must-have · **Estimate:** 4 SP · **Status:** Baseline
**Epic:** C – Privacy and Counsellor Profile · **Role:** Any user

## User outcome
Control profile visibility

## Acceptance summary
A user can select public, partially visible, or restricted profile visibility.

## Purpose
Support US-27 by letting a signed-in user choose public, partially visible or restricted profile visibility, so that Sam can seek advice without exposing more of his situation than he wants and David can keep his profile open to attract clients.

## Scope
- Privacy settings screen in the signed-in user's account area offering exactly three options: Public, Partially visible, Restricted, with a Save action.
- JWT-protected backend endpoints to read and update the authenticated user's own visibility setting; value constrained server-side to the three options.
- A stored per-account visibility state for both Job Seeker and Career Counsellor accounts, read back on every open of the screen.
- Loading, saved and error feedback states with English copy (NFR-08); success shown only after the backend confirms.

**Out of scope**
- Filtering what other users see according to the setting - US-28.
- Editing Job Seeker profile fields - US-29, outside the active backlog.
- Forum avatar-to-profile navigation - US-23..US-26, outside the active backlog.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a signed-in Job Seeker or Career Counsellor on the Privacy settings screen, when they tap Public, Partially visible or Restricted and tap Save, then the app shows the option as saved only after the backend confirms the update, and the same option is pre-selected after the app is closed and reopened.
- [ ] Given a user whose stored visibility is Restricted, when they open the Privacy settings screen, then the app pre-selects Restricted as returned by the backend rather than a default option.
- [ ] Given the backend rejects or fails the update, when the user taps Save, then the app shows an English error, keeps the previously stored option selected, and does not show a success state.
- [ ] Given a request with no valid session token or with a value other than public, partially visible or restricted, when the update endpoint is called, then the backend rejects it and the stored setting is unchanged.
- [ ] Given a signed-in user, when the update endpoint is called against a different user's account, then the backend rejects the request and that other user's setting is unchanged.

## Evidence
_Fill in when the story closes: link the PR, the tests and the device recordings that prove the acceptance criteria._
- [ ] PR: FE + BE changes merged into dev with this issue linked
- [ ] Tests: AT-US-27-1..AT-US-27-5 acceptance tests; BE unit tests for value validation, auth and ownership
- [ ] Recording: Privacy settings save, reopen and failure path on iOS and Android
- [ ] QA sign-off: comment listing the device/OS matrix used and results

## Dependencies
Blocked by: US-06 (#9)

## Sub-tasks
_Suggested split for the sub-team; convert to sub-issues at sprint planning._
- [ ] FE: Privacy settings screen with three options and save feedback
- [ ] BE: Get/update own visibility endpoints with value validation and auth
- [ ] QA: AT-US-27 on iOS and Android incl. failure and unauthenticated paths

## Assumptions and open decisions
- The exact profile fields exposed at each level are not defined in backlog.md or Requirements.md; the PO must agree one mapping used by both teams before this story is Ready (DoR).
- The default visibility for a newly registered account is not specified; to be decided with the PO before implementation.
- Platform Owner accounts are assumed to have no viewable profile and therefore no visibility setting.
- Australian Privacy Act handling and under-18 users (open decision, Project Background §7 item 8) are not addressed by this story.

issues.title: [US-28] Have privacy settings enforced
issues.body:
**Requirement ID:** `US-28`
**Priority:** Must-have · **Estimate:** 2 SP · **Status:** Baseline
**Epic:** C – Privacy and Counsellor Profile · **Role:** Any user

## User outcome
Have privacy settings enforced

## Acceptance summary
Other users receive only the profile fields allowed by the selected visibility setting.

## Purpose
Support US-28 by having the backend return, and the app show, only the profile fields allowed by the owner's visibility setting, so that Sam and Emily can trust that what they chose to hide stays hidden from other users.

## Scope
- Backend filtering of every profile read response by the owner's stored visibility level and the requester's identity, applied to every requester other than the owner (Requirements.md §4: front end respects privacy settings; backend is responsible for final authorisation enforcement).
- Profile view screen renders only the fields the backend returns and shows a clear restricted-profile state when the owner is Restricted.
- Owner exception: a user reading their own profile receives the full record.
- Applies to the counsellor professional profile (US-30). A Job Seeker's visibility setting (US-27) is enforced on any backend endpoint that returns Job Seeker account fields to another user.

**Out of scope**
- Choosing the visibility level - US-27.
- Marketplace listing and service-detail content - US-44 / US-46; how a Restricted counsellor appears there is an open assumption below.
- Forum-to-profile links - US-23..US-26, outside the active backlog.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a profile owner has set Public, when another user opens that profile screen, then the backend returns and the app shows every field defined as public for that profile type.
- [ ] Given a profile owner has set Partially visible, when another user opens that profile screen, then the backend response contains only the fields permitted at the partial level and the app shows nothing more, with omitted fields absent from the API response rather than hidden by the app.
- [ ] Given a profile owner has set Restricted, when another user opens that profile screen, then the app shows a clear restricted-profile state and the backend returns none of the restricted fields.
- [ ] Given a profile owner opens their own profile, when the screen loads, then the app shows their full profile regardless of the selected visibility.
- [ ] Given a profile owner changes their visibility via US-27, when another user opens the profile after the backend has confirmed the change, then the fields shown match the new level with no fields carried over from the previous level.

## Evidence
_Fill in when the story closes: link the PR, the tests and the device recordings that prove the acceptance criteria._
- [ ] PR: BE filtering + FE profile view merged into dev with this issue linked
- [ ] Tests: AT-US-28-1..AT-US-28-5; anonymous, wrong-user and owner API tests for all three levels (Requirements.md §4: front end respects privacy settings; backend is responsible for final authorisation enforcement)
- [ ] Screenshots: public, partial and restricted views of the same profile on iOS and Android
- [ ] QA sign-off: comment listing the device/OS matrix used and results

## Dependencies
Blocked by: US-27 (#22), US-30 (#24)

## Sub-tasks
_Suggested split for the sub-team; convert to sub-issues at sprint planning._
- [ ] BE: Filter profile responses by owner visibility level and requester
- [ ] FE: Render permitted fields only; restricted-state view
- [ ] QA: Cross-account API tests for all three levels; device check

## Assumptions and open decisions
- Uses the same field-per-level mapping agreed for US-27; it is not defined in the sources.
- How a Restricted counsellor appears in the public Marketplace listing and detail (US-44/US-46) is undecided; PO to confirm which listing fields stay public.
- The owner-sees-everything rule is inferred from the backlog wording 'other users receive only'; confirm with PO.
- Whether an unauthenticated user can open a profile screen at all is not defined; only Marketplace listing/detail (US-44/US-46) is confirmed public. PO to confirm; if public, the same filtering applies to anonymous requests.
- No baseline story defines a Job Seeker profile screen reachable by other users (US-23..US-26 and US-29 are excluded); PO to confirm whether one is needed for US-28 or whether Job Seeker privacy is enforced only at API level.

## Definition of Ready / Done
See `backlog.md` §6 and §7.

## Traceability
Baseline: `backlog.md` · Wiki: https://github.com/swen90014-2026-sm2/SWEN90014-2026-CSD-Koala/wiki/Requirements

issues.title: [US-31] Submit a LinkedIn profile for verification
issues.body:
**Requirement ID:** `US-31`
**Priority:** Must-have · **Estimate:** 4 SP · **Status:** Baseline
**Epic:** D – Counsellor Verification · **Role:** Career Counsellor

## User outcome
Submit a LinkedIn profile for verification

## Acceptance summary
A counsellor can submit a valid LinkedIn URL for Platform Owner review.

## Purpose
Support US-31 by letting a Career Counsellor submit a validated LinkedIn profile URL for manual Platform Owner review, so that David and Erika can start verification from their phone and Emily can later rely on counsellors who have been reviewed.

## Scope
- Verification screen for the signed-in counsellor with a LinkedIn profile URL field and a Submit action, reachable from first-login onboarding (US-05) and the account area.
- App-side and server-side URL validation with English feedback; the value must be a LinkedIn profile URL.
- JWT-protected submission endpoint that stores the URL against the counsellor's account with status pending.
- Role and ownership enforcement: only a Career Counsellor session can submit, and only for its own account.

**Out of scope**
- Platform Owner inspection and decision - US-58; status shown on profile and service-management views - US-32.
- LinkedIn sign-in, account linking or automated API verification - deferred: CLIENT-01 pending and R-01 (API does not expose what verification needs).
- Resubmission after rejection - open client question (25 Aug 2026, Q3); see assumptions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a signed-in Career Counsellor with no verification submission, when they enter a valid LinkedIn profile URL on the Verification screen and tap Submit, then the app shows the submission as Pending only after the backend confirms it has stored the URL with status pending.
- [ ] Given the URL field is empty or contains a value that is not a LinkedIn profile URL, when the counsellor taps Submit, then the app shows URL validation feedback in English and no request is sent or stored.
- [ ] Given an invalid URL bypasses the app and reaches the API, when the submission endpoint is called, then the backend rejects it with a validation error and no submission record is created.
- [ ] Given a Job Seeker session or an unauthenticated request, when the submission endpoint is called, then the backend rejects it and no submission is created.
- [ ] Given the backend fails during submission, when the counsellor taps Submit, then the app shows an error and does not show Pending until a later submission is confirmed by the backend.

## Evidence
_Fill in when the story closes: link the PR, the tests and the device recordings that prove the acceptance criteria._
- [ ] PR: FE + BE changes merged into dev with this issue linked
- [ ] Tests: AT-US-31-1..AT-US-31-5; BE unit tests for URL validation and role checks
- [ ] Recording: valid submission and invalid-URL feedback on iOS and Android
- [ ] QA sign-off: comment listing the device/OS matrix used and results

## Dependencies
Blocked by: US-04 (#7), US-06 (#9)

## Sub-tasks
_Suggested split for the sub-team; convert to sub-issues at sprint planning._
- [ ] FE: Verification screen with URL field and validation feedback
- [ ] BE: Submission endpoint storing URL as pending; role check
- [ ] QA: Valid/invalid URL and wrong-role tests on both platforms

## Assumptions and open decisions
- CLIENT-01 is pending: the baseline is URL submission plus manual review; if the client chooses LinkedIn sign-in or account linking, this story's inputs and AC change.
- Whether a rejected counsellor may edit and resubmit is an open client question (25 Aug 2026, Q3); R-02 proposes allowing it, but it is not built until confirmed.
- R-02's 'URL must match the registered name' is treated as a reviewer check under US-58, not an automated check here.
- 'Valid LinkedIn URL' means a syntactically valid LinkedIn profile URL; no live check against LinkedIn is performed.

## Definition of Ready / Done
See `backlog.md` §6 and §7.

## Traceability
Baseline: `backlog.md` · Wiki: https://github.com/swen90014-2026-sm2/SWEN90014-2026-CSD-Koala/wiki/Requirements

issues.title: [US-32] See the verification result
issues.body:
**Requirement ID:** `US-32`
**Priority:** Must-have · **Estimate:** 3 SP · **Status:** Baseline
**Epic:** D – Counsellor Verification · **Role:** Career Counsellor

## User outcome
See the verification result

## Acceptance summary
Relevant counsellor views consistently show pending, verified, or rejected status.

## Purpose
Support US-32 by showing the backend-held verification status (pending, verified or rejected) consistently on the counsellor's profile and service-management screens, so that David and Erika always know where their verification stands without contacting the platform.

## Scope
- Verification status (Pending / Verified / Rejected) displayed on the counsellor's Professional Profile screen and My Services screen, fetched from the backend on each load.
- JWT-protected read of the authenticated counsellor's own verification status.
- One shared status component and English label set so wording is identical on every counsellor view.
- Loading and error state when the status cannot be fetched; no status is guessed.

**Out of scope**
- Public verified badge on Marketplace counsellor information - US-46.
- Recording the decision - US-58; outcome of an additional investigation - US-33.
- Push or in-app notification of a status change - notification centre US-60 / US-61 is outside the active backlog.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a counsellor whose submission is pending, when they open the Professional Profile screen and the My Services screen, then both show Pending using the status returned by the backend.
- [ ] Given a Platform Owner has recorded Verified for the counsellor, when the counsellor next opens either screen, then both show Verified and neither shows a stale Pending state.
- [ ] Given a Platform Owner has recorded Rejected, when the counsellor next opens either screen, then both show Rejected with identical status wording on every counsellor view.
- [ ] Given the verification-status request fails, when a counsellor view loads, then the app shows an English error state and displays no status value until a later successful response from the backend.
- [ ] Given a signed-in counsellor, when the verification-status endpoint is called, then the backend returns only that counsellor's own status and rejects the request from a Job Seeker session.

## Evidence
_Fill in when the story closes: link the PR, the tests and the device recordings that prove the acceptance criteria._
- [ ] PR: FE status component + BE status read merged into dev with this issue linked
- [ ] Tests: AT-US-32-1..AT-US-32-5; BE tests for ownership and role on the status read
- [ ] Screenshots: Pending, Verified and Rejected on both screens, iOS and Android
- [ ] QA sign-off: comment listing the device/OS matrix used and results

## Dependencies
Blocked by: US-31 (#25), US-58 (#28), US-34 (#29)

## Sub-tasks
_Suggested split for the sub-team; convert to sub-issues at sprint planning._
- [ ] FE: Status component on Profile and My Services screens
- [ ] BE: Own verification status read endpoint
- [ ] QA: Verify all three statuses render identically across views

## Assumptions and open decisions
- The state before any submission is not one of the three statuses in the sources; the app is assumed to show a prompt to submit (US-31) - confirm with PO.
- Whether the rejection reason recorded under R-02 is shown to the counsellor is undecided.
- Status is refreshed on screen load; no notification is sent (US-60/US-61 excluded).

## Definition of Ready / Done

issues.title: [US-33] Receive the outcome of an additional manual investigation
issues.body:
**Requirement ID:** `US-33`
**Priority:** Should-have · **Estimate:** 4 SP · **Status:** Baseline
**Epic:** D – Counsellor Verification · **Role:** Career Counsellor

## User outcome
Receive the outcome of an additional manual investigation

## Acceptance summary
Completing an additional review updates the counsellor verification outcome consistently.

## Purpose
Support US-33 by letting a Platform Owner record the outcome of an additional manual investigation and propagating it to every counsellor view, so that David and Erika receive a single, current verification outcome after any re-review.

## Scope
- Platform Owner action on an already-reviewed or pending submission to record an additional-investigation outcome of pending, verified or rejected.
- JWT-protected backend endpoint that updates the counsellor's verification status and returns the new value; Platform Owner role enforced server-side.
- Counsellor views from US-32 (Professional Profile, My Services) show the updated status on next load.
- Validation and error feedback on the Platform Owner screen; the new outcome is shown as recorded only after backend confirmation.

**Out of scope**
- The initial approve / reject / leave-pending decision - US-58.
- Telling the counsellor the outcome changed - no notification centre (US-60 / US-61 outside the active backlog); the counsellor sees it on next open.
- Account suspension or broader account management - US-56 / US-57 / US-59, outside the active backlog.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a submission that already has a recorded outcome (pending, verified or rejected), when a Platform Owner records the result of an additional manual investigation, then the backend stores the new status and returns it as the counsellor's current verification status.
- [ ] Given the additional-investigation outcome has been stored, when the counsellor next opens the Professional Profile screen and the My Services screen, then both show the updated status and no view shows the previous one.
- [ ] Given the Platform Owner submits an outcome that is not pending, verified or rejected, when the endpoint is called, then the backend rejects it with a validation error and the counsellor's status is unchanged.
- [ ] Given a Job Seeker or Career Counsellor session, when the additional-investigation endpoint is called, then the backend rejects the request and the status is unchanged.
- [ ] Given the backend rejects or fails the update, when the Platform Owner confirms the outcome, then the app shows an error and continues to display the previously stored status as current.

## Evidence
_Fill in when the story closes: link the PR, the tests and the device recordings that prove the acceptance criteria._
- [ ] PR: BE status-update endpoint + FE Platform Owner action merged into dev with this issue linked
- [ ] Tests: AT-US-33-1..AT-US-33-5; BE state-transition and role tests
- [ ] Recording: outcome change propagating to counsellor views on iOS and Android
- [ ] QA sign-off: comment listing the device/OS matrix used and results

## Dependencies
Blocked by: US-58 (#28), US-32 (#26)

## Sub-tasks
_Suggested split for the sub-team; convert to sub-issues at sprint planning._
- [ ] BE: Additional-review outcome endpoint updating status; Platform Owner only
- [ ] FE: Platform Owner action to record re-investigation outcome
- [ ] FE: Counsellor views refresh to updated status
- [ ] QA: Status-change consistency tests across views and roles

## Assumptions and open decisions
- What triggers an additional investigation, its criteria and who gives final approval are undecided (25 Aug 2026 client question Q3).
- The Platform Owner console shape is an open decision (Project Background §7 item 3); assumed to be role-specific screens in the app (Requirements §1).

issues.title: [US-58] Review counsellor verification as a Platform Owner
issues.body:
**Requirement ID:** `US-58`
**Priority:** Must-have · **Estimate:** 4 SP · **Status:** Baseline
**Epic:** D – Counsellor Verification · **Role:** Platform Owner

## User outcome
Review counsellor verification as a Platform Owner

## Acceptance summary
A Platform Owner can inspect a submission and approve, reject, or leave it pending.

## Purpose
Support US-58 by giving the Platform Owner a verification queue where each LinkedIn submission can be inspected and approved, rejected or left pending, so that Emily, Jacob and Sam can rely on the verified status shown for counsellors like David and Erika.

## Scope
- Platform Owner Verification queue screen listing pending submissions with counsellor name and submitted LinkedIn URL; the URL opens the LinkedIn profile outside the app (R-02).
- Submission detail screen with Approve, Reject (optional reason, R-02) and Leave pending actions, each confirmed before sending.
- JWT-protected endpoints to list submissions, read one and record a decision; Platform Owner role enforced server-side.
- Status transitions pending to verified and pending to rejected stored by the backend and shown in the app only after confirmation.

**Out of scope**
- Forum moderation, reported-content and account-management consoles - US-56 / US-57 / US-59, outside the active backlog.
- Counsellor-facing status display - US-32; later re-investigation - US-33.
- Automated LinkedIn identity or qualification checks - deferred: CLIENT-01 pending, R-01.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a signed-in Platform Owner, when they open the Verification queue screen, then the app lists the pending submissions returned by the backend with each counsellor's name and submitted LinkedIn URL, and tapping the URL opens the LinkedIn profile outside the app.
- [ ] Given a pending submission is open, when the Platform Owner taps Approve and confirms, then the app shows Verified only after the backend stores status verified, and the submission no longer appears in the pending list.
- [ ] Given a pending submission is open, when the Platform Owner taps Reject and confirms, then the app shows Rejected only after the backend stores status rejected, together with any reason the Platform Owner entered.

issues.title: [US-69] Reschedule an upcoming booking safely
issues.body:
**Requirement ID:** `US-69`
**Priority:** Should-have · **Estimate:** 5 SP · **Status:** Baseline
**Epic:** F – Availability and Booking · **Role:** Job Seeker or Career Counsellor who is a participant in the order

## User outcome
Reschedule an upcoming booking safely

## Acceptance summary
An authorised participant can move an eligible confirmed booking to another open slot without duplicating the order or losing the original on failure.

## Purpose
Support US-69 by letting an authorised order participant move an eligible confirmed booking to another open slot through one backend operation that keeps the original booking if anything fails, so that Jacob can shift a session around work and Erika can move a clash without either losing the booking or paying twice.

## Scope
- Reschedule action on an eligible upcoming confirmed booking, available to the Job Seeker and the counsellor of that order
- Slot picker reusing the open-slot rules of US-40 for the same counsellor and service
- Backend reschedule endpoint that releases the old slot and reserves the new one on the same order, creating no new order or booking
- On any failure the original booking and slot remain unchanged and the app shows the failure
- Updated time reflected in confirmation, My Bookings and booking details after the backend confirms

**Out of scope**
- Cancellation, refunds, reschedule deadlines and fees — policy is open (background §7 item 7)
- Notifying the other participant (notification centre outside the active backlog, US-60/US-61)
- Rescheduling past, cancelled or unpaid bookings

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a confirmed upcoming booking, when its Job Seeker or counsellor taps reschedule, then the app shows only that counsellor's currently open slots as selectable.
- [ ] Given the participant selects an open slot and confirms, when the backend completes the reschedule, then the same order and booking reference show the new time, the old slot is open again, the new slot is unavailable, and no second order or booking exists.
- [ ] Given the chosen slot was reserved by someone else first, when the backend processes the reschedule, then it rejects the request, the booking keeps its original slot, and the app shows the failure without presenting the move as done.
- [ ] Given the backend fails part-way through the operation, when the booking is re-read, then exactly one booking exists and it still holds its original slot, the new slot is not reserved by it, and no second order or booking exists.
- [ ] Given a user who is not a participant, or a booking that is past, cancelled or not confirmed, when a reschedule request is sent, then the backend rejects it and the booking is unchanged.

Review a completed purchased service

## Acceptance summary
An eligible buyer can submit a one-to-five-star rating and written comment from a completed order.

## Purpose
Support US-53 by letting the buyer of a completed order submit a one-to-five-star rating and written comment for that service, so that Emily and Sam can record their experience and later Job Seekers such as Jacob can rely on feedback that comes only from verified buyers.

## Scope
- App: review action on the Job Seeker's completed order and a review screen with a one-to-five star selector and a written comment field
- Backend: submit-review endpoint that validates the rating is an integer from 1 to 5, requires a valid JWT, and enforces that the caller is the buyer of an order in completed state
- Backend: stored review linked to the order, service, counsellor, and author so US-54 and US-55 can aggregate it
- App: review shown as submitted only after backend confirmation; validation and backend errors displayed

**Out of scope**
- Updating the service average, count, and review list: US-54; counsellor overall rating: US-55
- Editing or deleting a review, counsellor replies to reviews, and review reporting or moderation: no baseline story (moderation console US-56/US-57 is outside the active backlog)

- [ ] Given a logged-in Job Seeker is the buyer of an order in completed state, when they open that order and tap the review action, then the app shows a review screen for that service with a one-to-five star selector and a written comment field.
- [ ] Given the buyer selects a rating from 1 to 5 and enters a comment, when they submit, then the app shows the review as submitted only after the backend confirms it was stored against that order and its service.
- [ ] Given the rating is missing or outside 1 to 5, when the buyer submits, then the backend rejects the request with a validation error, the app displays it, and no review is stored.
- [ ] Given an order that is not in completed state (for example confirmed but not yet delivered, or cancelled), when the buyer views it, then no review action is offered and a direct API submission for that order is rejected by the backend.
- [ ] Given a user who is not the buyer of the order (another Job Seeker, the counsellor, or a Platform Owner), when they submit a review for that order via the API, then the backend rejects it with an authorisation error.

## User outcome
See updated service-level feedback

## Acceptance summary
A submitted review updates the service average, count, and review list consistently.

## Purpose
Support US-54 by updating a service's average rating, review count, and review list on the backend whenever a review is stored and showing those values on the service detail screen, so that Emily can validate a service against real buyer reviews before purchasing and David can monitor feedback on each of his listings.

## Scope
- Backend: service detail response includes the average rating, review count, and review list (star rating and comment) recalculated from stored reviews after each confirmed submission
- App: service detail screen (US-46) renders average, count, and list from the backend and refreshes after returning from review submission

- Counsellor-level overall rating on profiles and listings: US-55
- Marketplace filtering and sorting by rating: US-45

- [ ] Given a service has no reviews, when its detail screen loads, then a clear no-reviews state with a zero count is shown and no rating value is fabricated.
- [ ] Given a review submission was rejected by the backend, when the service detail is viewed afterwards, then the average, count, and list are unchanged.
- [ ] Given the review list is displayed, when a viewer reads an entry, then it shows the star rating and written comment exactly as returned by the backend.
